note: One good article (PubMed, BJA and similar) for each academic question Apoorva asks Claude. Kept for 7 days, then removed.

items.title: International consensus statement on the management of hypotension with vasopressors during caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia
items.why: The standard reference for phenylephrine at caesarean: infusion rates, bolus doses, BP targets and handling bradycardia.

items.title: New-onset atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy for cancer.
items.why: Short free review on why AF happens after oesophagectomy, its link with leak and pneumonia, and how to work it up.

items.title: Peri-operative approach to esophagectomy: a narrative review from the anesthesiological standpoint.
items.why: Free review covering pre-op risk, OLV and protective ventilation, fluids, monitoring and analgesia for open and minimally invasive oesophagectomy.

items.title: Physiological and anatomical changes of pregnancy: Implications for anaesthesia.
items.why: System-by-system walk-through of pregnancy changes with the anaesthetic point for each – a good single read for the viva.

items.title: Strong ions, weak acids and base excess: a simplified Fencl-Stewart approach to clinical acid-base disorders.
items.why: The anaesthesia paper behind bedside base-excess partitioning (Na−Cl−38, 0.25 × (42 − albumin)) used in the ABG notes.

items.title: Fourth universal definition of myocardial infarction (2018).
items.why: The source of the current ST elevation, ST depression and pathological Q-wave cut-offs used to call an MI on the ECG.

items.title: The arterial tourniquet: pathophysiological consequences and anaesthetic implications.
items.why: Classic anaesthesia review of local and systemic effects of inflation and deflation, tourniquet pain and safe use.

items.title: Drug-receptor interactions in anaesthesia.
items.why: Leicester opioid-receptor group explaining receptor types, GPCR signalling, agonists, partial agonists and antagonists, with opioid examples.

items.title: Valvular heart disease and anaesthesia.
items.why: Haemodynamic goals for each valve lesion, including why filling, rate and rhythm matter so much in mitral stenosis.

items.title: Tunneled Hemodialysis Catheter Insertion: Technical and Clinical Considerations
items.why: Short primer on when to choose a tunnelled vs non-tunnelled dialysis line, site choice, tip position and complications.

items.title: Management of mitral stenosis: a systematic review of clinical practice guidelines and recommendations
items.journal: Eur Heart J Qual Care Clin Outcomes
items.why: Side-by-side summary of the major guidelines: when to use balloon valvotomy, when to send for surgery, and medical/antibiotic therapy.
